name: Pelvic tilt
summary: Lying with knees bent, flatten the lower back into the floor by tilting the pelvis, then release.
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Tighten the stomach and press the lower back down so the pelvis rocks back. Hold, then let the natural curve return.
why: The pelvis rocks a few degrees under clothing — invisible to a phone. Logged by hand.
progression: Progress to a dead bug or bridge.
regression: Fewer reps; a pillow under the head.
contraindications: None in most cases — this is usually the first back exercise.

faults.label: Pushing through the feet
faults.tip: Pressing the heels down tilts the pelvis for you. The stomach should do it.

faults.label: Squeezing the buttocks instead
faults.cue: Use the stomach, not the bottom
faults.tip: The tilt comes from the abdominals pulling the pelvis; the buttocks stay soft.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: The exhale helps the stomach draw in.

faults.label: No hold at the end
faults.tip: The hold is what teaches the control; a quick flick teaches nothing.

points.t: Rocks back; the lower back flattens.
